title: Open nonconformance
purpose: Open the nonconformance of a complaint ticket: a new record with Complaint as its source, linked to the ticket.
summary: Open a nonconformance for a complaint, from its ticket. The record gets Complaint as its source and stays linked to the ticket. The ticket's assignee or a supervisor does this.

tasks.title: Open a nonconformance for a complaint
steps: On the complaint's ticket, select [[Open nonconformance]] in the Complaint section.
Write a [[Title]] and [[What happened]] in your own words and choose the [[Severity]].
Add the [[Area or section]] and any [[Containment]], then select [[Open nonconformance]].

tasks.title: Get the new record worked
steps: The record opens after saving. A supervisor chooses its owner there with [[Choose owner]].

good_to_know: Nothing is copied from the ticket. Every staff role reads the record while the ticket may be restricted, so write it without patient names or identifiers.
A complaint has at most one nonconformance. If it already has one, this page takes you to it.
While a review of the complaint counts, opening one here is refused. Raise a nonconformance from the list and link the ticket instead.
The record starts without an owner, even when a supervisor opens it.
The complaint's ticket stays linked to the record and cannot be removed from it.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: This page exists only if your laboratory uses the optional nonconformance module; otherwise it answers Not found. The ticket must be one you may open and must be a complaint, otherwise the page answers Not found. Only the ticket's assignee or a supervisor (the admin role included) may open a nonconformance from it; anyone else is refused. It opens from the Complaint section of the ticket page, as a dialog or a full page.

sections.title: Fields and actions
paragraphs: A No patient data notice heads the form, followed by a line naming the complaint, for example Opened from complaint REQ-000123. Its source is Complaint, and the ticket is linked to the new record. Nothing is copied from the ticket. There is no Source or Owner field.

items.label: What happened
items.description: Required, up to 4,000 characters. What was found, where and when.

items.label: Severity
items.description: Required: Minor, Major or Critical. The laboratory's own grading.

items.label: Containment
items.description: Optional, up to 4,000 characters. What was done at once to limit the problem.

items.label: Open nonconformance
items.description: Creates the record in status Open with source Complaint and no owner, links the ticket, adds Nonconformance NC-000123 opened from this complaint to the ticket's timeline, confirms Nonconformance NC-000123 opened. and opens the record.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to the ticket without opening anything.

items.label: Ticket version
items.description: The form carries the version of the ticket you opened it from. If the ticket changed meanwhile, saving is refused with your input kept: This ticket changed. Reload it and review the latest entries. Opening the record also advances the ticket's version, so other forms open on that ticket must be reloaded.

items.label: After the review
items.description: When the complaint's review counts, saving is refused: This complaint has been reviewed; its record no longer changes. Raise a nonconformance and link the ticket instead.

items.label: One per complaint
items.description: If the complaint already has a nonconformance, opening this page goes to that record with This complaint already has a nonconformance. A save that meets one opened at the same moment is refused the same way.

items.label: On the ticket
items.description: Once the record exists, the ticket's Complaint section shows it as the corrective action, for example NC-000123 · Open, and the Open nonconformance button is no longer offered.

items.label: Signed out by a time limit
items.description: When a time limit signs you out, what you typed here is kept for 24 hours, for you in that browser only, and comes back on this page when you sign in again there (a form open in a dialog opens again on its own page). It keeps the version of the ticket you typed against: if the ticket changed since, the page says This record changed after you typed it, and saving is refused with your typing on the form, also when the complaint's record was opened meanwhile. Copy what you need, then select Discard on the notice, or after a refused save go back to the ticket.
